newsitem.title: LATVIA: MINISTER SEES INTENTIONAL SELL-OFF IRREGULARITIES.
newsitem.headline: MINISTER SEES INTENTIONAL SELL-OFF IRREGULARITIES.

text.p: Latvia's Economy Minister Guntar Krasts blasted the Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) on Friday, saying that he sees intentional irregularities in the sell-off process.

"Last September I had to endure severe criticism from a high ranking World Bank official for the incomprehensible and misterious privatisation of the Savings Bank (Krajbanka)," Krasts told a news conference.
Krasts mentioned the merger of the Savings bank with "the ailing Riga Union Baltic Bank, which is at the moment eating up its own capital".
"Privatisation voucher accounts, opened in the Savings bank, open the way for large-scale machinations," Krasts said.
Krajbanka, currently on the privatisation list and the fifth largest Latvian bank, merged with the UBB in February.
Krasts said that a similar criticism could be directed against the privatisation of Latvian Gas and all other big projects.
When asked about Latvian Gas, in which German and Russian companies signed strategic investor agreements earlier this week, Krasts referred to Gaz de France.
"You should ask Gaz de France. They would tell you, what was suggested to them and why in the LPA," Krasts said.
"Latvian Gas privatisation was almost wrecked or given a completely wrong direction," he added.
As both German and Russian strategic investors were worried about Latvian Gas debts, the taking of its stake was delayed since last autumn.
The LPA said earlier this year that Gaz de France might be offered a Latvian Gas stake if the German side would back out of the deal.
Krasts was also critical of two of the current LPA managers whom he refused to name.
Krasts added that local small and medium- sizeed businesses were not being suficiently involved in the privatisation process.
"LPA takes the easiest way, strengthening the (positions of) big capital in Latvia," Krasts said.
